subject: SLOs & SLA wording follow-up: latency measurement, exclusions, reporting cadence
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLOs & SLA wording follow-up: latency measurement, exclusions, reporting cadence

Hi Sara —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps focused on performance/SLO confirmation and the SLA language you asked us to draft. I captured our notes below; please flag anything I missed.

1) Performance targets you asked us to qualify (examples shown as p95 unless noted):
   - Text generation (<=512 input tokens, <=256 output tokens): p95 latency target 150 ms
   - Throughput: steady-state 2,000 requests/sec for the service tier in scope
   - Concurrency: support for 500 concurrent active sessions with KV caching enabled
   - Streaming: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) p95 target 80 ms; delta-token emit latency p95 target 50 ms

2) Measurement scope & assumptions we discussed:
   - Measurements from Redwood ingress (edge) to Redwood egress (first token / last token) unless otherwise noted.
   - Typical test load will be a mix of 70% short chat requests and 30% long-form generation; we can provide synthetic traffic profiles.
   - Cold-starts, scheduled maintenance windows, and customer-driven backend calls (your downstream enrichment) are common exclusions; we should explicitly list these in SLA language.

3) Reporting & remedies you requested:
   - Monthly performance report (percentiles, error rates, sample traces) delivered within 3 business days after month close.
   - Raw percentile CSV available on request for audit.
   - Remedies: service credits for monthly SLO misses (TBD % by severity).

Next steps (proposed):
   - Aditya (SE) will follow up with exact measurement definitions and example telemetry points.
   - We (Marissa) will draft proposed SLA wording that spells out measurement method, exclusions, reporting cadence, and a sample credit table. Draft attached.
   - Schedule 30-min follow-up with your infra/ops + our SE to align on test harness and a scoped concurrency test next week.

Attachments: redwood-slo-proposal-draft.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

--
Redwood Inference | Developer-first LLM inference platform

From: Sara Park <sara@acmecloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Matthew Lee <matthew.lee@acmecloud.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLOs & SLA wording follow-up: latency measurement, exclusions, reporting cadence

Marissa —

Thanks for the summary, this is helpful. A couple clarifying Qs from our side before we move to formal wording: 

1) Measurement point: when you say "ingress to egress" can you confirm whether that includes network transit to our VPC endpoint or if it's measured inside Redwood's control plane only? For compliance we need to be explicit about network-related variability.

2) Exclusions: you mentioned cold starts and maintenance windows — can you provide proposed maximum duration per month for scheduled maintenance that would be excluded (e.g., 2 hours/month)? Also, how do you propose handling customer-initiated load spikes that cause downstream backpressure?

3) Remedies: our procurement team will want a clear credit table (e.g., <99.9% p95 = 10% credit, <99% = 25%, etc.). Can you propose a starting point?

We can share an initial list of internal telemetry (what we can provide) before the test.

Thanks — Sara
Sara Park
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Cloud
sara@acmecloud.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 00:10:00 -0800
Subject: RE: SLOs & SLA wording follow-up: latency measurement, exclusions, reporting cadence

Sara —

Quick technical clarifications from SE perspective so procurement has specifics to work with. Below are proposed definitions we usually surface in SLAs; happy to adjust to your needs.

Measurement definitions:
- "Latency" (generation): measured as time from Redwood API ingress (when request is accepted by our edge) to the time the last byte of the response is emitted from Redwood egress. For streaming, we provide both TTFB (time from ingress to first byte emitted) and completion latency (last byte).
- Percentiles: we report p50, p90, p95, p99 over 5-minute rolling windows and aggregate for monthly reporting. The SLA will reference p95 over the monthly aggregated traffic for the account's plan.

Exclusions (proposed):
- Scheduled maintenance windows (we propose up to 2 hours/month excluded; longer windows will be agreed in advance).
- Emergency maintenance (we will notify and provide root cause after the event).
- Customer-side network outages or third-party downstream failures (we ask Acme to provide correlation IDs / traces to attribute).
- Cold starts for model variant scale-ups: define cold-start window as first 30s per model instance scaled during a burst; we can exclude a capped amount of cold-start occurrences per month (e.g., first 100 cold-start events).

Measurement/verification:
- Redwood will publish a monthly CSV containing timestamped percentiles and error rates. For audit purposes, we can provide sample request/response traces (redacted) and a summary of synthetic-run test results.

Reporting cadence & remedies (proposed):
- Monthly performance report delivered within 3 business days after month close.
- Remedy table (example - subject to legal review):
   * If monthly p95 <= target: no credit.
   * If monthly p95 > target for > 60 minutes total aggregated: 10% service credit on monthly invoice.
   * If monthly p95 > target for > 180 minutes aggregated: 25% credit.
   * If platform is unavailable (error-rate > 5% across > 30 minutes): 50% credit up to a cap of 100% for prolonged outages.

Note: the above credit thresholds are our starting recommendation. We typically refine thresholds and caps with procurement/legal to align with contract philosophy.

If this looks reasonable, Marissa and I can draft the exact SLA paragraphs and a redline-ready credit table.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

Thanks for the detail, Aditya. A few asks from procurement/ops before we proceed to redline:

1) Please provide a short sample SLA paragraph that explicitly states the latency measurement definition (we'll use that as the canonical clause in our procurement redline).
2) Can you confirm the format of the monthly report (CSV columns, percentile timestamps) and whether raw percentile histograms are available? We may ask for automated delivery into a shared GCS bucket.
3) Remedies: procurement would like an initial credit table proposal in plain text (we saw your suggested table but need concrete %s tied to exact measured windows).

If you can send a one-page draft SLA + the sample CSV header and example row, we'll loop legal. Also, can we get a 30-minute slot next Tue (1/13) morning PST for an ops test-scope sync?

-Matt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: SLOs & SLA wording follow-up: latency measurement, exclusions, reporting cadence

Excellent — thanks for the fast replies. Attached is a 1-page draft SLA paragraph (redwood-slo-proposal-draft.pdf) and a CSV template for the monthly report (appended in the mutual-action-plan.xlsx). Key callouts/responding to your asks:

- Canonical sample SLA paragraph (excerpt):
  "Latency for text-generation is measured from the time the request is accepted by Redwood's ingress (edge) to the time the last byte is emitted from Redwood's egress. For streaming responses, Redwood reports Time-to-First-Byte (TTFB) and completion latency (last byte emitted). Percentiles (p50, p90, p95, p99) are computed over 5-minute rolling windows and aggregated for the monthly report. Scheduled maintenance (up to 2 hours/month), customer-controlled network outages, and defined cold-start windows (first 30s per instance scale event, capped at 100 events/month) are excluded from SLA calculations."

- CSV header provided: timestamp_utc, metric_name, p50_ms, p90_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, error_rate, request_count, sample_traces_link

- Remedies (concrete proposal to start negotiations):
   * If monthly p95 <= target: 0% credit.
   * If monthly p95 > target for > 60 minutes aggregated across the month: 10% credit on monthly invoice.
   * If monthly p95 > target for > 180 minutes aggregated: 25% credit.
   * If error rate > 5% for > 30 minutes aggregated: 50% credit up to a maximum of 100% in exceptional prolonged outage cases.

Next steps:
  - Aditya: finalize the sample paragraph and include the exact telemetry keys we'll publish.
  - Marissa/Dylan: propose 3x 30-min slots next Tue (1/13) morning PST; I'll send a calendar invite once Matthew confirms availability.
  - Sara/Matt: share any constraints on scheduled maintenance windows or additional exclusions you want us to consider.

Attachments: acme-slo-questions.docx (your Qs), redwood-slo-proposal-draft.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to the ops sync.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
